items.detail:
The new annotation lumps both earlier flips together as "metadata corrections of a dropped date". That fits the GLM 4.5V annotation, which calls itself "a metadata correction on an otherwise unchanged row". It does not fit the Kimi K2.5 annotation immediately above it, which says "It matters more than a badge" and records that the derived catalog and the joined entry now disagree about the same model — a live inconsistency, not a correction. Both flips were indeed dropped expiration dates, so nothing here is false about the data; the contrast clause just flattens a record this same file already carries. "both of which were dropped expiration dates, not new deprecations" would say the true part without re-characterising the Kimi case.

items.detail:
The annotation reads "a real lifecycle event, since OpenRouter serves no status field of its own." The subordinate clause does not establish the main one — that OpenRouter ships no status field explains why the status is *derived*, not why this particular flip is *real* rather than a metadata correction. The sibling annotation on the same source (j-20260901-08, the nex-n2-mini row) carries the reason that actually does the work: "unlike the two earlier status flips on this source, which were metadata corrections of a dropped date." I confirmed the substance is sound either way — `data/changes.jsonl` holds exactly two lines mentioning `nex-n2-pro` (the `field_change` at l.114 and this annotation), so no prior status flip on this row could have been a correction — so this is a wording fix, not a claim defect.

items.detail:
The proposal's evidence line carries "CyberGym 84.5 vs GLM-5.2 77.2; ExploitGym 105/130 vs 29/39". Fetching https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3 on 2026-09-01 confirmed the GLM-5.3 side — license "glm-5.3", 753B params, the "Emergent Cyber Capability" note, CyberGym 84.5, ExploitGym 105/130 — but the extraction surfaced a second ExploitGym row (130/247 at a 6-hour timeout) and did not surface either comparator (77.2, 29/39). The "29/39" denominator matches neither 130 nor 247, so the pair may be reading across two different timeout rows. WebFetch's extractor is not evidence of absence, so this is not a finding that the numbers are wrong — it is that the post job must read the benchmark table itself, state which timeout row each figure comes from, and name the card as the cited document, rather than inheriting the pair from this proposal.
